correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite-second-moment Borel probability measures, the potential-interaction energy decomposes exactly into the mean-mode energy \(a_i m_i^2/2\) and centered-mode energy \(b_i v_i/2\). A selected affine Wasserstein pushforward changes those modes by the squares of \(1-\eta_i a_i\) and \(1-\eta_i b_i\). A pathwise visit-count identity gives the exact finite-time binomial expectation, and the simultaneous coordinate-frequency strong law gives the almost-sure exponent for every nonzero initial measure. Dirac and symmetric two-atom laws attain the modal extremes. Scalar equioscillation uniquely optimizes the steps, harmonic probability equalization gives the two different minimax samplers, and strict monotonicity of \(-\log t/(1-t)\) yields the exact coincidence condition. A strictly positive two-coordinate family proves near-stagnation of expected energy under the almost-sure optimizer. The actual standalone verifier passed 1,197 exact-rational checks, plus numerical logarithmic and limiting-regime checks. Finite computations only supplement the universal analytic proof.

title: Annealed and almost-sure optimal sampling diverge for interacting Wasserstein coordinate descent

value.rationale: The exact annealed/quenched two-risk frontier answers a natural fixed-sampling design question for recent coordinate Wasserstein descent across all dimensions and finite-second-moment laws. Its mean-versus-centered decomposition and unique optimal-probability classification show that expected and almost-sure improvements require different allocations even for strictly convex interacting quadratic energies. In the boundary family \(\beta_1\downarrow0\), the almost-sure-optimal rule has worst-case expected factor tending to one, whereas the expected-optimal factor tends to \(4/7\). This sharp risk conflict informs interpretation of typical runs against expected guarantees; no wider nonlinear or non-diagonal consequence is asserted.
